netbird_not_installed: Not installed. The NetBird client {version} is downloaded from GitHub to the KVM and checked against a pinned checksum.

netbird_target_active: The computer gets {address} on its USB adapter when it renews its address or USB reconnects. NetBird peers reach it there, and see its traffic from that address.
netbird_target_dns: DNS: the computer is given {server} as a DNS server. Names under {zone} resolve through NetBird; other names through the KVM's DNS servers.
netbird_target_intro: The target computer becomes its own NetBird peer: the KVM runs the peer for it and hands its NetBird address to the computer over USB. Nothing is installed on the computer.
netbird_target_key_description: A setup key for the computer's peer, from the same NetBird account as this KVM. It is used once and not stored.
netbird_target_needs_kvm: Join this KVM to NetBird first; the target's peer uses the same server, and the KVM's NetBird address becomes its gateway.
netbird_target_waiting: Waiting for both peers to connect; until then the computer gets a short local lease.
netbird_usb_not_shared: To make the computer on USB Ethernet its own NetBird peer, choose NetBird as the USB Ethernet mode.
netbird_usb_shared: USB Ethernet is in NetBird mode: the computer on it can be its own NetBird peer.

network_discovery_check_help: Sends ARP probes from 0.0.0.0, as a device does before taking an address, so no device learns a wrong mapping. Works for any address on the same network segment.
network_discovery_intro: Runs on the KVM, from its network port.
network_discovery_item_description: Find hosts on a subnet, see the KVM's neighbor table, and check whether an address is taken.
network_discovery_method_arp_help: Asks each address of the subnet by ARP. Every IPv4 device on the same network segment must answer, even if its firewall drops ping. Does not reach other subnets behind a router.
network_discovery_method_ipv6_help: Pings all IPv6 nodes on the link at once (ff02::1) and adds the IPv6 neighbor table. Windows does not answer this ping by default and shows only once it is in the neighbor table.
network_discovery_method_ping_help: Sends a ping to each address. Also reaches subnets behind a router, but devices that drop ping stay hidden.
network_discovery_neighbors_help: The KVM's ARP (IPv4) and NDP (IPv6) table: devices it talked to recently.

os_services_guide_headless_intro: On a server or single-board computer nobody signs in to a desktop, so the service needs these steps instead. Steps 1 and 3 run as root, the others as the user. The clipboard needs a desktop and stays off.

os_services_guide_headless_step_allow: As the user, allow this KVM:
os_services_guide_headless_step_boot: As the user, start the service at boot instead of with a desktop session:
os_services_guide_headless_step_linger: As root, keep the user's services running without a sign-in:
os_services_guide_headless_step_run: Switch to the user, point systemctl at the user's session, and run the AppImage:
os_services_guide_headless_step_usb: As root, install the USB access rule and give the user the KVM's USB device. The packaged rule only covers a local desktop session:
os_services_guide_intro: Install OS Services on the computer the KVM is connected to, as the user who signs in there. Choose its system and architecture.
os_services_guide_item_description: Steps for Windows, macOS and Linux, for each architecture.
os_services_guide_linux_fuse: FUSE to open the AppImage (fuse3 on Debian and Ubuntu), or run it with --appimage-extract-and-run.
os_services_guide_linux_glibc: glibc 2.35 or newer: Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, Fedora 36 or newer.
os_services_guide_linux_no_dialogs: Without zenity there are no dialogs. Install the access parts from a terminal instead:
os_services_guide_linux_step_installed: The service now runs from ~/.local/share/ipkvm-os-services and starts at each sign-in. You can delete the AppImage.
os_services_guide_linux_step_run: Run the AppImage as the desktop user, not as root:
os_services_guide_linux_step_signout: Sign out and sign in again, so capture gets the new group membership.
os_services_guide_linux_step_usb: At Allow USB access?, click Allow USB Access and enter an administrator password. This installs the USB access rule and the capture helper.
os_services_guide_linux_video_arm: For video the service needs a VAAPI H.264 encoder, which most ARM boards lack. The KVM then shows its HDMI capture; the terminal, files and host info still work.
os_services_guide_linux_video_x86: For video: the VAAPI, EGL and GLES libraries with a VAAPI H.264 driver (Intel, AMD), or NVENC on NVIDIA in a Wayland session. Without them the service still runs and the KVM shows its HDMI capture. On Debian and Ubuntu:
os_services_guide_macos_step_drag: Open the DMG and drag IP-KVM OS Services to Applications.
os_services_guide_macos_step_open: Open IP-KVM OS Services from Applications. It starts the service, which then starts each time you sign in.
os_services_guide_macos_step_recording: Allow Screen Recording when macOS asks, or turn on IP-KVM OS Services in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording. Without it the KVM shows its HDMI capture.
os_services_guide_which_macos: Apple menu > About This Mac: a chip named Apple M… is Apple silicon; an Intel processor is Intel.
os_services_guide_which_windows: Settings > System > About shows the system type. There is no build for Windows on Arm.
os_services_guide_windows_step_run: Run the installer as the user who signs in. It installs the service for that user, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\IP-KVM OS Services, and starts it.
os_services_guide_windows_step_signin: The service then starts each time that user signs in.
os_services_host_info_description: Show the target computer's system information, process names and USB devices to whoever uses this KVM.

os_services_install_media_busy: Unmount the current virtual media, then try again.
os_services_install_mounted: Installer mounted. Open the disc on the target computer.
os_services_install_no_card: Insert a TF card into the KVM. The offline installer is saved to the card first.

os_services_repository_custom_help: A folder laid out like JetKVM's server: releases.json, <version>/ with each release's files, and jetkvm-os-services.iso.
os_services_repository_description: Where OS Services releases come from: the offline installer disc the KVM downloads and mounts, the installer disc's download link, and updates
os_services_repository_github_help: Release assets: files of a version come from the release tagged with that version (for example 0.3.1/IP-KVM-OS-Services_0.3.1.iso), the newest offline disc (jetkvm-os-services.iso) and the update index (releases.json) from the latest release.
os_services_repository_http_private: The repository URL must be https, or http with a private or loopback IP address.
os_services_repository_signature_note: Updates are installed only when they carry a signature the KVM trusts (JetKVM's key). The installer disc and its downloads work with any repository.
os_services_resolution_description: Apps on the target computer can change the current resolution.
os_services_save_failed: Failed to save OS Services settings: {error}
os_services_setup_description: Mount the installer, run it on the target computer, then allow the fingerprint.
os_services_terminal_description: Open a shell as the desktop user.
os_services_terminal_macro_and: Run the next command if the previous one succeeded
os_services_terminal_macro_example: Example: restore "tmux attach -t work %QUIET%" hides tmux's "no sessions" message before start runs.
os_services_terminal_macro_intro: Use these in the start and restore commands; the KVM replaces each with the form for the terminal type, so one command works in every shell. Restore and start are joined with %OR%.
os_services_terminal_macro_or: Run the next command if the previous one failed
os_services_terminal_macro_quiet: Hide the previous command's error messages
os_services_terminal_macro_sep: Run the next command in any case
os_services_terminal_mux_description: Run a terminal multiplexer in each new browser terminal, so programs keep running when the terminal is ended or the browser disconnects and come back in the next one. MCP and Terminal API shells stay plain.
os_services_terminal_mux_help: Each new browser terminal gets "restore %OR% start" typed once its prompt appears: the restore command runs first, and the start command only when restoring fails. The multiplexer must be installed on the target and on the shell's PATH.
os_services_terminal_mux_preset_descript: Fills both commands for a known multiplexer; edit them as needed.
os_services_terminal_mux_rex_note: Rex documents a command to create a session (rex new) but none that attaches a plain terminal to one, so the restore command is empty: each new terminal starts a new Rex session. Fill in a restore command if your Rex version has one.
os_services_terminal_shell_command_help: Typed first into each new browser terminal to start another shell, e.g. pwsh -NoLogo on Windows or fish on macOS. Leave empty for the target's default shell: the user's login shell on macOS and Linux, Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows. With Auto-detect, a shell named here sets the terminal type.
os_services_terminal_shell_description: The shell of the browser terminal; the commands the KVM types are written for it.
os_services_terminal_shell_reason_comman: Commands are written for {name}, which the shell command below starts.
os_services_terminal_shell_reason_os: Commands are written for {name}, the default shell on {os}.
os_services_terminal_shell_reason_settin: Commands are written for {name}, as set here.
os_services_terminal_shell_reason_unknow: The target has not reported its system yet (host info), so commands are written for a {name}.
os_services_video_confirm_off_descriptio: The picture comes from the HDMI input again. The video reconnects.
os_services_video_confirm_on_description: The picture comes from OS Services on the target instead of HDMI. The video reconnects.

usb_device_wake_description: Lets the KVM wake the sleeping target over USB (the Wake button when there is no HDMI signal). Always present, so its endpoint is permanently reserved. Not Wake-on-LAN.
usb_endpoints_note: The USB controller has 9 IN endpoints. IN 6 and IN 8 lose data, so when a function would land on one, that endpoint is reserved (striped) and the function moves up; OS Services takes 1 when it is on.
usb_endpoints_over: {used} needed, the controller has {total}: turn something off

wifi_networks_remove_description: The device no longer joins this network.
